# definednet_tag (Resource)

Manages a tag. Tags are `key:value` labels applied to hosts; a tag can carry nebula config overrides, route subscriptions, and additional inbound firewall rules.

Tags are addressed by name, so changing `name` replaces the resource. Tag priority is managed by the API: use `before` or `after` to position a tag relative to another one.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "definednet_tag" "dev" {
  name = "env:dev"
}

resource "definednet_tag" "prod" {
  name        = "env:prod"
  description = "Production hosts"

  # Give prod higher precedence than dev for config overrides.
  after = definednet_tag.dev.name

  # Values are JSON: use jsonencode() for every type.
  config_overrides = [
    { key = "lighthouse.dns.host", value = jsonencode("0.0.0.0") },
    { key = "lighthouse.dns.port", value = jsonencode(53) },
    { key = "definednet.dns.resolver_addrs", value = jsonencode(["10.0.0.53"]) },
  ]

  # Every host with this tag is subscribed to the datacenter route.
  route_subscriptions = [definednet_route.datacenter.id]

  firewall_rules = [
    {
      protocol     = "TCP"
      description  = "node exporter from monitoring hosts"
      allowed_tags = ["role:monitoring"]
      port_range   = { from = 9100, to = 9100 }
    },
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Tag in `key:value` form. Key is at most 20 characters, value at most 50, no surrounding whitespace. Changing it forces a new tag.

### Optional

- `after` (String) Position this tag after the named tag (higher precedence than it). Sent on create and whenever `before` or `after` changes; the API does not report it back, so it is not detected as drift. Conflicts with `before`.
- `before` (String) Position this tag before the named tag (lower precedence than it). Sent on create and whenever `before` or `after` changes; the API does not report it back, so it is not detected as drift. Conflicts with `after`.
- `config_overrides` (Attributes Set) Nebula config overrides applied to hosts with this tag. `value` is JSON, so use `jsonencode()`: `jsonencode("info")` for a string key, `jsonencode(4242)` for a number, `jsonencode(["10.0.0.1"])` for a list. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--config_overrides))
- `description` (String) Optional description, at most 255 characters.
- `firewall_rules` (Attributes Set) Inbound firewall rules applied to hosts with this tag, in addition to their role's rules. At most 50. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--firewall_rules))
- `route_subscriptions` (Set of String) Route IDs every host with this tag is subscribed to. At most 100.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Same as `name`; tags have no separate ID.
- `priority` (Number) Precedence assigned by the API. Overrides from a higher priority win over lower ones.

<a id="nestedatt--config_overrides"></a>
### Nested Schema for `config_overrides`

Required:

- `key` (String) Dotted nebula config key, e.g. `lighthouse.dns.host`.
- `value` (String) JSON-encoded value for the key.


<a id="nestedatt--firewall_rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `firewall_rules`

Required:

- `protocol` (String) Protocol to allow: `ANY`, `TCP`, `UDP`, or `ICMP`.

Optional:

- `allowed_role_id` (String) Only allow hosts with this role. Omit to allow every role.
- `allowed_tags` (Set of String) Only allow hosts carrying every one of these `key:value` tags. Omit to allow any tags. An empty set means the same thing to the API as omitting the attribute and is always reported back as null, so it is rejected to keep the plan and refreshed state in agreement.
- `description` (String) Optional description, at most 255 characters.
- `port_range` (Attributes) Inclusive port range. Omit to allow every port. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--firewall_rules--port_range))

<a id="nestedatt--firewall_rules--port_range"></a>
### Nested Schema for `firewall_rules.port_range`

Required:

- `from` (Number) First port in the range (1-65535).
- `to` (Number) Last port in the range (1-65535). Must be at least `from`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import definednet_tag.prod env:prod
```
